Ashford Sanitation Department

(A) ______

Starting July 1, large household items such as sofas, beds, and refrigerators will be collected by reservation only. Items left on the street without a reservation will not be picked up, and their owners may be fined.

How it works:
1. Reserve a pickup date on the department's website or by phone at 555-0163.
2. Pay the collection fee. Fees range from $3 to $15 depending on the size of the item.
3. Print the confirmation sticker and attach it to the item.
4. Place the item in front of your building after 8:00 p.m. on the evening before your pickup date.

■ Working appliances can be donated instead; our reuse center will collect them for free.
■ A reservation can be canceled for a full refund until noon on the day before pickup.

Not Sure Whether to See a Doctor?

When you or a family member feels unwell late at night, it can be hard to decide what to do. CareLine 24 is a free telephone service that connects you with a registered nurse at any hour, every day of the year.

Our nurses listen to your symptoms and give you __sound__ advice based on approved clinical guidelines. They can tell you whether to care for yourself at home, visit a clinic the next day, or go to an emergency room right away. They can also help you find the nearest pharmacy that is open.

Please note that our nurses cannot diagnose illnesses or prescribe medicine. CareLine 24 is not an emergency service. If someone has chest pain, trouble breathing, or severe bleeding, call an ambulance immediately.

Keeping Your Meals Safe

The Lakemont Food Safety Office works to make sure that food sold in our city is safe to eat. Our inspectors __conduct__ unannounced checks at more than 2,000 restaurants, school kitchens, and markets each year. They look at how food is stored, how clean the kitchen is, and whether workers wash their hands properly.

HomeCare Visit Program (Elmsworth Public Health Center)

Health Care That Comes to Your Door

For older residents who live alone, a trip to a clinic can be difficult. Through the HomeCare Visit Program, nurses from the Elmsworth Public Health Center visit them at home.

During each visit, a nurse checks blood pressure and blood sugar, reviews the medicines the resident is taking, and looks for safety risks such as slippery floors. Nurses also take time to listen. If a resident has concerns about memory loss, poor appetite, or loneliness, the nurse works with doctors and social workers to __address__ them.

The program is free for residents aged 65 or older who live alone or have a chronic illness. Visits are made once a month, or more often when needed.

Family members and neighbors may apply on a resident's behalf. To apply, call 555-0191 or ask at any community service center.

Stop Smoking Clinic
Corbridge Public Health Center

Thinking about quitting? You are far more likely to succeed with support. Our Stop Smoking Clinic offers a free six-month program for anyone who lives or works in Corbridge.

What we provide:
■ A one-on-one meeting with a counselor on your first visit
■ A breath test to measure carbon monoxide

■ Follow-up text messages and phone calls

Those who stay smoke-free for six months receive a small gift.

Halden Government Complex, Building A

Before you swim

Maple Grove Animal Care Center

The Maple Grove Animal Care Center is the city's only public shelter for lost and abandoned animals. Each year we take in about 1,500 dogs and cats and work to return them to their owners or find them new homes.

What we do
- Lost and found: Animals brought to the center are kept for ten days while we search for their owners. Photos are posted on our website within 24 hours.
- Adoption: Animals are examined by a veterinarian, vaccinated, and microchipped before adoption. The adoption fee is $40 for dogs and $25 for cats.
- Education: We visit schools to teach children how to care for pets responsibly.

Adopters must be at least 19 years old and attend a one-hour class before taking an animal home.

Visiting hours: Tuesday – Sunday, 1:00 p.m. – 5:00 p.m.
opts: It is one of several public animal shelters in the city.
It keeps lost animals for a month while looking for owners.
It charges the same adoption fee for dogs and cats.
It requires adopters to take a class before adoption.
exp: 입양하려는 사람은 동물을 데려가기 전에 한 시간짜리 교육을 받아야 한다고 했으므로 입양 전 교육을 요구한다는 말이 일치한다. 이곳은 시에 하나뿐인(only) 공공 보호소이고, 들어온 동물은 주인을 찾는 열흘 동안 보호하며, 입양비는 개 40달러, 고양이 25달러로 다르다.

Using the Reading Room
Wexmoor City Archives

The Wexmoor City Archives keeps the city's official records, maps, and photographs. Anyone may view them in the Reading Room free of charge.

Hours: Monday – Friday, 9:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.

How to use the Reading Room
1. Register at the front desk with a photo ID. A visitor card is issued on the spot.
2. Request materials using the computers in the lobby. Up to five items may be requested at a time, and requests close at 3:30 p.m.
3. Put your bags and coats in a free locker. Only pencils, notebooks, and laptops may be taken inside.

Handling the records
■ Wear the gloves provided when touching photographs.
■ Photos may be taken without flash for personal study.
■ Copies cost 20 cents per page.

Materials may not be taken out of the room.
opts: 열람실은 주말에도 이용할 수 있다.
자료는 한 번에 다섯 점까지 신청할 수 있다.
열람실 안에서 펜으로 필기할 수 있다.
자료를 사진으로 찍는 것은 금지된다.
exp: "Up to five items may be requested at a time"이라고 했으므로 자료를 한 번에 다섯 점까지 신청할 수 있다는 말이 일치한다. 열람실은 월요일부터 금요일까지만 열고, 안에는 연필, 공책, 노트북만 가지고 들어갈 수 있어 펜은 쓸 수 없으며, 개인 연구를 위한 사진은 플래시 없이 찍을 수 있다.

Citywide Earthquake Drill

The City of Verano will hold its annual earthquake drill so that everyone knows what to do when the ground shakes.

Date: Wednesday, October 20
Time: 2:00 p.m. – 2:20 p.m.

What will happen:
■ At 2:00 p.m., sirens will sound for one minute and a test alert will be sent to mobile phones.
■ People indoors should get under a sturdy table and hold on until the siren stops.
■ After the siren, walk to the nearest open space using the stairs. Do not use elevators.
■ Drivers should pull over to the right side of the road for five minutes. Subway trains will run as usual.

Dunmore District Office

When: The first and third Wednesday of every month, 2:00 p.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Where: Consultation Room, 1st floor, Dunmore District Office

Interpreter Services for Patients
Calloway University Hospital

Clear communication is part of good care. Patients who are not comfortable speaking English can ask for a medical interpreter at no charge.

Languages: In-person interpreters are available in Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese, and Arabic. For over 40 other languages, we use video interpretation on a tablet.

Hours: In-person interpreters work on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Video interpretation is available 24 hours a day.

How to request:
■ Tell the staff when you make an appointment, or ask at the International Desk on the 1st floor.
■ For planned visits, please request an in-person interpreter at least three days in advance.

For your safety, family members under 18 should not interpret medical information. Interpreters keep everything they hear private. They help with consent forms and discharge instructions, but they cannot give medical advice.
